recorded: 2026-09-27, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook), Gemma 4 26B-A4B UD-Q4_K_XL public-path shape matrix
purpose: Baseline shape matrix for the gfx1151 Gemma 4 campaign: separated prefill, decode, first-token and public-wall numbers on the public LLM.generate() path, with the artifact and harness provenance needed to compare against llama.cpp and against later hipEngine revisions. A coverage record, not a promotion claim: the campaign's gfx1100 rows are untouched.

artifact.quant_mix: 29 of 30 layers are (gate/up Q4_K, down Q5_1); layer 29 is (gate/up Q5_K, down Q8_0). 128 experts, top-8, hidden 2816, expert ffn 704, 16 heads / 8 kv (2 on every 6th layer), head_dim 512, sliding window 1024.

protocol.timing: prefill_s is forward(prompt) plus an explicit device synchronize, and first_token_s is the same boundary measured through the public path; decode_s covers the remaining forwards after the first token; public_wall_s is the end-to-end request wall time on LLM.generate(). Decode throughput is decode_forwards / decode_s, and the public-wall figure explicitly includes prefill.
protocol.parity: public_path_parity compares the harness's public-path token ids against the direct-runner ids for the same request; it is true on all five rows.

comparator.limits: the comparator covers one shape (512/128) on the same host and artifact; no llama.cpp row exists for the other four shapes, and llama-bench's pp512 is a prefill-only measurement rather than the harness's first-token boundary.

reading.prefill_scales_sublinearly: prefill throughput falls from 122.50 tok/s at 128 prompt to 77.22 at 4096 (-37%), so a per-token cost grows with prompt length. That is consistent with the compact-row gather, the attention prefill pass and the KV write all scaling with rows, and is the first thing to attribute when optimizing for long prompts.
reading.decode_falls_with_context: decode throughput falls from 21.96 to 17.58 tok/s across the same range (-20%), which tracks the attention pass's key walk.
reading.wall_is_prefill_dominated: at every row except 128/128 the public wall is dominated by prefill: 4.24 s of 10.30 s at 512/128 and 53.04 s of 61.14 s at 4096/128.

context.how_this_tree_got_here: three units landed on the gfx1151 host before this measurement: the Q5_1 expert down projection moved to a weight-reusing grouped prefill (2048/8 prefill 39.82 -> 48.57 tok/s), the Q4_K gate/up followed (512/128 55.34 -> 92.57 tok/s, 2048/8 48.84 -> 75.17 tok/s), and the Q4_K kernel then got staged activations plus hoisted weight metadata (512/128 92.28 -> 121.90 tok/s). This host's 512/128 prefill was 11.617 s before those units and is 4.240 s in this matrix.
context.known_remaining: the Q5_1 down projection has not had the staged-fetch treatment (23.0% of prefill kernel time), and Q8_0 dense projections (12.5%) plus attention prefill (12.2%) follow it.

scope.gfx1151_only: every number here is gfx1151. No gfx1100 row is qualified, changed or compared by this artifact.
scope.single_request: all rows are single-request, greedy, fixed length, context 8192, BF16 KV. No served-path row, no multi-request row, and no speculative/MTP row is included.

provenance.bench_artifacts: /tmp/t5-128p128o.json, /tmp/t5-512p128o.json, /tmp/t5-1024p128o.json, /tmp/t5-2048p8o.json, /tmp/t5-4096p128o.json (each carries the harness's own provenance block, including git state, artifact bytes and head sha256, rocm-smi clock/power, and the full HIP*/HSA*/ROCR* environment); the llama.cpp comparator output is /tmp/llamacpp-gemma4-baseline.md. Raw logs are not committed.
